note: The grove's people are tools/worlds/homelands.json's (West Toxxulia): Elder Silverbough gives the first two, Thornwarden Briony beside her the three hunts; Weaver Fernlight (a few steps south of the elder) is the outfitter, Coachman Thistlewick, a satyr of the eastern woods, keeps the stable on the shore to the north. The hunts are all in the woods west of the lake: the bark beetles nearest, the rootcoil snakes deeper in, the rotting shambler Rotbark alone at the far west edge. The flight sets a ranger or druid down in Surefall Glade and the rest in Qeynos.

L1.name: An Acorn for the Ear
offer: A new leaf on the old tree! Every dryad of the grove wears an acorn cap at her ear, from the oak that first sheltered us, so the forest knows her voice.
Weaver Fernlight keeps them. She sits by the water a few steps south of here.
Will you fetch your acorn cap and show it to me?
L1.declined: The grove is patient, little leaf.
L1.started: Go, then. Fernlight is by the water, just south of here.

piece.name: acorn-cap earring
piece.description: The cap of an acorn from the grove's first oak, hung on a thread of bark. Every young dryad of the grove wears one.

fetch.journal: Ask Weaver Fernlight, south of Elder Silverbough, for an acorn-cap earring.
fetch.says: Silverbough sent you? Turn your head, little leaf. There: a cap from the first oak. The grove asks nothing for it but that you come back.

show.journal: Show the acorn-cap earring to Elder Silverbough.
show.says: It suits you. Wear it, and the old trees will know your step wherever you walk.

L2.name: Rooted in the Grove
offer: The wind carries young leaves far, and not all of them land softly. Have Spiritmaster Ashleaf bind your spirit to the grove, so that you wake here if you fall.
Then give your name to Coachman Thistlewick for his ledger. His coach runs to Freeport and to the other homes of the Homelands, for those their stables know.
Will you see them both and come back to me?
L2.declined: Then stay under the branches until you do.
L2.started: Both are north along the shore: Thistlewick the satyr first, Ashleaf a little past him.

bind.journal: Have Spiritmaster Ashleaf, north of the elder along the shore, bind your spirit to the grove.
bind.says: It is done. Should you fall, you will wake here under our branches. Now go and give Coachman Thistlewick your name.

ledger.journal: Give your name to Coachman Thistlewick, on the shore north of the elder, for his ledger.
ledger.says: Welcome to my stable, little leaf. My coach runs to Freeport and to every other home of the Homelands, for travelers whose names their ledgers hold. Yours is in mine now.

says: Good. Now your roots are here, however far your branches reach.
Thistlewick's coach will carry you to Freeport if its ledger knows you, but the way west to Qeynos is earned. Thornwarden Briony, beside me, has work for you.

L3.name: Beetles in the Bark
offer: So you are the new leaf. Good. Bark beetles are boring into the old trees in the woods west of the lake, and the trees are sickening.
Stop them and bring me three of their shells. Then I will teach you something worth knowing.
Will you hunt them?
L3.declined: Then the old trees will suffer.
L3.started: Three shells. The trees will thank you.

drop.name: bark beetle shell
drop.description: The shell of a bark beetle from the woods west of the dryads' lake.

hunt.journal: Take three bark beetle shells from the bark beetles in the woods west of the lake.

give.journal: Bring three bark beetle shells to Thornwarden Briony.
give.says: Three shells, and not a leaf out of place. You can fight. Now watch closely, and learn this.

L4.name: A Sapling's Arms
offer: Soft bark will not serve you among the humans. I will make you proper gear, but you will fetch what I need.
Weaver Fernlight has bark cord and a shaft of deadfall for me. Then take a skin from the rootcoil snakes deeper in the woods to the west, past the beetles.
Will you bring me all three?
L4.declined: Then keep to the grove, and to its shade.
L4.started: Cord and a shaft from Fernlight, a skin from the snakes. Go.

items.name: willow-bark cord
items.description: A cord of willow bark, peeled and twisted by the weavers of the dryads' grove.

materials.journal: Ask Weaver Fernlight for the willow-bark cord and the wooden shaft.
materials.says: For Briony? Here, a cord of willow bark and a shaft of deadfall. No living branch was cut for it: tell her so.

drop.name: rootcoil snake skin
drop.description: The mottled skin of a rootcoil snake from the deep woods west of the dryads' lake.

hunt.journal: Take a rootcoil snake skin from the rootcoil snakes deep in the woods west of the lake, past the beetles.

give.journal: Bring the willow-bark cord, the wooden shaft and the rootcoil snake skin to Thornwarden Briony.
give.says: All three. Give me a moment... there. It is yours: let it serve the forest.

L5.name: Rotbark
offer: One task more before you go west. A shambler of the forest has gone to rot at the far west edge of the woods. We call it Rotbark, and what it touches withers.
It stands alone there, past the snakes, and it strikes at anything that walks. Bring me its heartwood, and I will teach you the last thing I have for a sapling.
Will you hunt Rotbark?
L5.declined: The rot will not wait as you do.
L5.started: West through the woods, past the beetles and the snakes. Do not let it take hold of you.

drop.name: Rotbark's heartwood
drop.description: A knot of blackened heartwood from the rotting shambler Rotbark.

hunt.journal: Take Rotbark's heartwood from the rotting shambler Rotbark at the far west edge of the woods.

give.journal: Bring Rotbark's heartwood to Thornwarden Briony.
says: Rotbark's heartwood... The woods can heal now. You are a sapling no longer.
Learn this, and see Gatekeeper Thornwyn when you are ready to go west.

flight.name: Roots in the West
offer: The way to Tunaria is open. The humans of Qeynos guard the groves of Surefall Glade, where our rangers and druids go; the rest of us train in Qeynos itself.
You have earned the passage, sapling. I will set you down among your own guild there, and your spirit will rest there.
Shall I send you west?
flight.declined: The way will wait for you.
flight.journal: Tell Gatekeeper Thornwyn when you are ready to go to Qeynos.

L7.name: The Pines of the Eyrie
offer: The homes keep a hunters' outpost under the Goldfeather Eyrie, and the few pines round it are dying. Drift rats gnaw their bark, and badgers dig out their roots.
Ride Thistlewick's coach there. Bring me two drift rat teeth and a badger's claw from the snow east of the outpost, so the pines can rest.
Will you guard the Eyrie's pines?
L7.declined: The pines will wait as long as they can.
L7.started: Thistlewick's coach will take you. Wrap up, little leaf: it is cold.

drop.name: drift rat incisor
drop.description: A yellow gnawing tooth from a drift rat of the Goldfeather Eyrie's snow.

hunt.journal: Take two drift rat incisors from the drift rats east of the Eyrie outpost.

drop.name: snowfield badger claw
drop.description: A long digging claw from a snowfield badger of the Goldfeather Eyrie.

hunt.journal: Take a snowfield badger claw from the badgers on the snow east of the Eyrie outpost.

give.journal: Bring the drift rat incisors and the badger claw to Thornwarden Briony.
give.says: Teeth and a claw. The pines will heal by spring. The forest is kind to those who keep it. Now watch closely, and learn this.

L10.name: Thorn and Silk
offer: You have grown past a sapling's arms. I will make you a thornwarden's weapon, bound with silk that does not rot in rain or snow.
Weaver Fernlight has cord for the grip. Then bring me two skeins from the rime spiders north-east of the Eyrie outpost.
Will you bring me the cord and the silk?
L10.declined: Then your old arms will serve a while longer.
L10.started: Fernlight first. Then the spiders, and mind their webs.

items.name: willow-bark cord
items.description: A cord of willow bark, peeled and twisted by the weavers of the dryads' grove.

materials.journal: Ask Weaver Fernlight in the grove for willow-bark cord.
materials.says: Cord for Briony again? Here, from the same old willow. She asks nothing of a tree it cannot spare.

drop.name: rime spider silk
drop.description: A skein of frosted silk from a rime spider of the Goldfeather Eyrie.

hunt.journal: Take two skeins of silk from the rime spiders north-east of the Eyrie outpost.

give.journal: Bring the willow-bark cord and the rime spider silk to Thornwarden Briony.
give.says: Willow and silk. A moment... there. It is yours: let it serve the forest, wherever you carry it.

L13.name: The Balance of the Snow
offer: An old snow leopard they call Old Frostjaw hunts the slopes north-east of the Eyrie outpost. He kills more than he can eat, and the snow is emptying of game.
A forest is kept by taking what is out of balance. Bring him down, and I will teach you what a thornwarden knows. Take friends.
Will you bring down Old Frostjaw?
L13.started: He strikes first. Let the others draw him, and strike when he turns.

hunt.journal: Kill Old Frostjaw on the slopes north-east of the Eyrie outpost.

back.says: He is gone? Then the game will come back to the slopes, and the hunters will eat. That is balance. Learn this.

L15.name: A Seed of Ice
offer: The Rimeheart walks the ice caves north-east of the Eyrie outpost, and where it walks nothing grows. The elder wants it broken, and a piece of it brought here.
We will bury the shard under the old oak. Even ice that never melts gives way to roots in time.
Will you bring me a shard of the Rimeheart?
L15.declined: Then the caves stay barren a while longer.
L15.started: Do not go into those caves alone, little leaf.

drop.name: shard of the Rimeheart
drop.description: A shard of blue ice that never melts, broken from the Rimeheart.

hunt.journal: Take a shard from the Rimeheart, in the ice caves north-east of the Eyrie outpost.

give.journal: Bring the shard of the Rimeheart to Thornwarden Briony.
give.says: So cold, even now. The oak will have it, and a hundred springs will soften it. You have done the grove proud. Learn this.

L20.name: The Last Pines
offer: Briony says your roots are deep now. Before a dryad of the grove chooses her path, she does a kindness for the homes we share the land with.
Spiritmaster Oswin at the Eyrie outpost sent word on the wind: the raiders are cutting the last pines. Go to him, then come home to me.
Will you go to Oswin?
L20.declined: The pines cannot wait forever, little leaf.

road.journal: Find Spiritmaster Oswin at the Eyrie outpost.
road.says: Silverbough's word reached you? Good. The Goldfeather raiders cut the pines for their fires. Warden Halvek means to stop them: go to him.

road.journal: Find Warden Halvek at the Eyrie outpost.
road.says: Oswin sent you. The raiders round the eyrie east of here carry war-talons. Bring me three, and they will learn the pines are guarded.

drop.name: Goldfeather war-talon
drop.description: A war-talon of the Goldfeather aviaks, bound in gold thread.

hunt.journal: Take three war-talons from the Goldfeather raiders round the eyrie east of the Eyrie outpost.

handin.journal: Bring the three war-talons to Warden Halvek.
handin.says: Three talons. The pines will stand another winter. Go home to your grove: your elder will want to hear it from you.

final.journal: Return to Elder Silverbough in the grove.
final.says: You left a sapling and came back with branches that shelter other homes. The grove has one more thing to give you.
